One price for a card is usually the wrong price

Asking what a trading card is worth without saying which copy is like asking what a used car costs. The answer depends on the printing, the condition, and whether it has been graded.

Card AI prices the specific copy. Raw cards are broken out by condition, graded cards by grading company and grade, so a PSA 10 and a lightly played raw copy of the same card never share a number.

Price history matters more than the current price

A single current price tells you what the market thinks today. It does not tell you whether that price has doubled over six months or is sliding after a reprint announcement.

Card AI keeps price history and market trends on individual cards, which is what you need to decide between selling now, holding, or buying more.

Two ways to use the card price scanner

  • Scan the card with your camera, review the suggested catalog matches, and confirm the printing details
  • Run a card price lookup by name, set or card number when you do not have the card in hand

Both routes land on the same catalog record with the same pricing and history. That makes the trading card value app useful whether the copy is on the table or only on your want list. From price check to portfolio

Checking one card is useful once. The value compounds when the cards you check become a tracked collection with a running total that updates as the market moves, so you know what the whole thing is worth without re-checking card by card.

Because the card price database sits behind every entry, a card price scanner result and a text lookup resolve to the same number.

Published prices and marketplace research

These are separate questions.

  • A price guide summarizes the available market price for a printing
  • A card valuation applies a raw condition or existing slab grade to the copy you own
  • A marketplace search helps you inspect listings and research comparable sales yourself

Card AI shows published current prices and available price history for the selected card record. For supported sports cards, it provides a link to an eBay search using the card name, set and number. It does not import eBay sold transactions or calculate the published market price from that search.

Tracking prices after the check

Checking a card once answers a question. Watching it answers a better one.

Cards in your collection carry price history, so a card value tracker is built in rather than bolted on: you can see what your holdings did over time, not just what they are worth today. The collection total moves with them.

Card price checker questions.

How is a card price scanner app different from a price lookup?

Scanning starts from a photo and suggests likely catalog matches for you to confirm. A price lookup starts from a name, set or card number. Both routes open the same confirmed card record with the same available current price and history.

What is this card worth?

Select the matching catalog record, confirm its finish and language, and choose a raw condition or existing slab grade. Card AI then shows the relevant market price and available price history.

Can I use Card AI as a Pokemon card value checker?

Yes. Search by Pokemon name, set or card number, confirm the exact printing, then choose the raw condition or existing slab grade. Card AI shows the selected record's available published price and history.

Can I get a Pokemon card valuation on this website?

Use the website’s text lookup to find a matching Pokémon card record and its available published price. Check the source, condition or existing grade, language, finish and observation date. This is a reference, not an appraisal of an uploaded photo or a guaranteed sale price.

Are the public guide prices in my local currency?

The guide tables label their samples in USD and show each price date. When comparing another market or currency, check the currency, date, printing and condition first. Shipping, fees and individual offers can differ from a published reference.

Why is the graded price so different from the raw price?

Raw condition and an existing grading-company grade identify different price comparisons. Choose the matching context and date; a raw Near Mint copy is not automatically equivalent to a PSA grade.

Do I need to scan a card to check its price?

No. Search the card catalog by name, set or card number and open a matching record to see its current market price, price history and details.

Is this a card price guide or a valuation tool?

The website provides published price references for exact records. Card AI can help track confirmed holdings. Neither workflow guarantees a sale price or independently appraises the condition of your physical copy.

What is my card worth if it is a TCG card in poor condition?

Raw cards are valued by condition band, so a played copy is not priced as a near-mint one. Being honest about condition gets you a number closer to what the card actually sells for.

Can I get card price alerts when a value moves?

Price history is kept per card and the collection total revalues as the market moves, so changes are visible when you open the collection. Card AI does not currently send automatic price-movement alerts.

Can I search eBay from a sports card record?

Yes, supported sports card records can link to an eBay search based on the card name, set and number. Check listings and any sold-item filters on eBay itself; Card AI does not import sold transactions into its price feed.

Can I check a price without downloading Card AI?

Yes. Use the website’s text price lookup. Photo scanning and personal holdings are separate app workflows.
